slint-interpreter 1.18.1 from crates.io with four changes (the second and fourth need vendor/i-slint-core), the first two in ItemTree::item_geometry (search for "Telescope patch"): ItemTree::item_geometry no longer clones
the item's geometry expression and no longer builds a Struct from it.

Why: Slint asks every item for its geometry on every walk of the item tree (rendering, hit testing, dirty tracking). The interpreter answered by cloning the
whole geometry expression (a deep copy of an expression tree, allocating) and evaluating it into a Value::Struct (a HashMap of SmolStr to Value, allocating
again), then read x, y, width and height back out of the map. A profile of the desktop window at 4K with every plugin loaded showed that walk at about 46 %
of the window thread, malloc, free and memmove at about 40 % of it.

What it does now: the expression is borrowed from the compilation unit (the cell is only borrowed while it is read, as before), and when it is the usual
Expression::Struct the four fields are evaluated one by one, in the order upstream gets them from the field map (height, width, x, y), because evaluating height can create a ComponentContainer's component, which x reads. Any other expression shape takes the old path, so results are the same. The dependencies the
evaluation reads are tracked exactly as before, because the same sub-expressions are evaluated in the same context.

Second change, in item_tree_vtable.rs and instance.rs (search for "Telescope patch"): ItemTree::item_geometry now remembers each item's rect. Instance has one cache entry per flat tree index
(created on first use) holding the last rect and a PropertyTracker. The geometry is only evaluated again when the tracker is dirty, that is when a property the geometry expression read has changed;
the tracker is registered as a dependency of whatever is being evaluated (the window's redraw tracker, a layout), so a change reaches them as it did before. One difference from upstream's other caches: evaluating an item's geometry can itself invalidate a property it already read (a ComponentContainer creating its component sets properties), and
PropertyTracker::evaluate_as_dependency_root forgets such a change because it clears the dirty flag after the closure. The vendored i-slint-core has a variant that clears it before (see
vendor/i-slint-core/PATCH.txt), so the tracker is still dirty afterwards. The cache evaluates once; while the tracker is dirty again it evaluates again, at most 8 times in one query. If it has not settled after 8 passes nothing is cached
for that query: the geometry is evaluated once more directly in the caller's own tracking context, exactly as without the cache, and the entry stays dirty so the next query starts over.
Nothing guarantees such a chain ever settles; it just costs what it cost before the cache. An ordinary item is evaluated once. The renderer (femtovg has no
partial rendering) still walks every item that is not inside a cached layer on each frame, so this makes each visit cheap instead of making fewer visits. Items in a repeated row live in their own
Instance, so a repeater adding or removing rows never reuses an entry for a different item.

Measured (release, window thread CPU over 40 s after 25 s warm-up, fake phone, headless nested KWin, one run each):
  4K, everything loaded and on:  15.77 % -> 13.32 % (15 % less)
  4K, nothing loaded:             3.75 % ->  3.15 % (16 % less)
  1080p, everything loaded and on: 12.77 % -> 10.25 % (20 % less)
  1080p, nothing loaded:          2.80 % ->  2.37 % (15 % less)
The main window and the Settings window drew byte for byte the same before and after.

Measured with the cache on top (same setup, two runs each, base then patched back to back): 4K all on 13.5 -> 11.5 %, 4K nothing loaded 3.1 -> 3.1 % (no change, within noise), 1080p all on 10.3 -> 8.6 %, 1080p nothing loaded 2.2 -> 1.85 %.
Pixels: the main window, Settings, a resize, and a card folding and unfolding (mid-animation too) drew byte for byte the same.

Third change, in item_tree_vtable.rs and instance.rs (search for "Telescope patch"): ItemTree::parent_node and sub_component_path_of no longer search the tree on every call.

Why: the core asks for an item's parent on every walk (absolute positions, hit testing, dirty tracking). For an item in a repeated row the interpreter found the row's place in its parent by walking
the parent's whole sub-component tree for the path and then scanning dynamic_table for the matching repeater, each time. After the geometry cache this was about 15 % of the window thread at 4K
with everything on (Instance::parent_node 8.1 % and sub_component_path_of 7.2 % self time).

What it does now: the tree of one instance never changes after build_instance (repeaters and conditionals put their rows in their own Instance, and sub_components is filled once), so where a
sub-component sits below its root is found once and kept in SubComponentInstance::path_in_root, and a repeated Instance keeps the flat index of its placeholder in the parent in parent_flat_index
(only set when the lookup succeeds). Embedded components (ComponentContainer) and popups take the same path as before. resolve_item_rc_from_ref uses the same cached path.

Measured (release, window thread CPU over 40 s after 25 s warm-up, everything on, two runs each, base then patched back to back): 4K 11.3 -> 9.9 %, 1080p 8.8 -> 7.0 %.
Pixels: main window, three window sizes, folding and unfolding cards drew byte for byte the same.

Drop it with the rest of this folder.

Fourth change, in instance.rs (search for "Telescope patch"): Instance::ensure_instantiated only walks its repeaters, conditionals and ComponentContainers when something they read has changed.

Why: the core runs ensure_instantiated on the whole tree before every frame and every input event. Each call went through every dynamic node of every instance, cloned Rc's and the
compilation unit for each, read each repeater's model property and collected each repeater's rows into a fresh Vec to recurse into them, even when nothing had changed. After the
parent lookup cache this was the largest interpreter cost left on the window thread at 4K with everything on (Instance::ensure_updated 6.9 % and PropertyHandle::update for the model 4.2 % self time).

What it does now: every Instance with dynamic nodes has a PropertyTracker that records what its last walk read (the models, the repeaters' dirty flags, the conditions, a ListView's
viewport and row heights, the ComponentContainer's factory). A child instance's tracker is registered with its parent's before the child walks, so a change anywhere below marks every
instance above it dirty, and a clean instance answers straight away. The walk uses the keeping-invalidation variant from vendor/i-slint-core, so a change the walk itself causes (a row's
init setting a property another repeater's model reads) leaves the tracker dirty for the next call. A ListView sets its dirty flag without reading it, so the walk registers it
explicitly. A walk that re-enters the same instance (from init code) walks as before without the tracker. Direct ensure_updated calls (get_subtree_range, get_subtree) are unchanged.
Rows still appear, update and go in the same call as before: the tracker only skips walks that would have changed nothing.

Measured (release, window thread CPU over 40 s after 25 s warm-up, everything on, two runs each, base then patched back to back): 4K 9.9 -> 8.4 %, 1080p 7.0 -> 6.5 %.

Drop it with the rest of this folder.

Drop it when Slint stops cloning and boxing in item_geometry (nothing upstream is known yet; check the release notes after 1.18.1), then remove this folder and the
slint-interpreter line under [patch.crates-io] in rust/Cargo.toml. Tests and the lockfile were left out of the copy, and so were the [[test]] entries for them in Cargo.toml.
Slint's GPL-3 option is what Telescope uses; the licence files are kept in LICENSES.
